findings.finding: ‘We partly replicated the planning findings of Kupzyk (2011)’ gives an immediate aggregate verdict. The rest of the first sentence names the main source findings, followed by replay scope and numerical results.

findings.location: Section 1, opening paragraph continuing onto p. 2
findings.finding: ‘We partly replicated Kupzyk’s headline findings’ opens the section. The paragraph then specifies the reconstructed samples, unavailable replay inputs, paired contrasts, ICC pattern, and thresholds before explaining the general design.

The introduction defines the three kinds of power and the results give concrete comparisons and explanations in manuscript prose. The short ‘Disagreement record’ identifiers accompany rather than substitute for explanations.
The appendix explains the two regeneration routes in prose and commands.

The observed summary is internally compatible with a partial scientific verdict: allocation and dropout dominate size effects, ICC .05 maximizes the five losses but the skewed-size case is nonmonotone, and the extreme thresholds and rejection rates differ.
The visible coverage map runs from Chapter I motivation through Appendices A–D, with separate entries for the formulae, power grids, contrasts, oversampling, thresholds, and practical planning.
The observed-count degrees-of-freedom extension, independent-mask estimand, and proxy for unobserved source Monte Carlo uncertainty are explicit.
Five unresolved comparisons name the distinguishing unavailable inputs. The source and rerun software availability are separately described.
The finite same-outcome comparison separates a refitting contribution from shrinking simulation error and leaves general equivalence unresolved.
Numerical agreement at the printed precision is a separate column from scope, and the prose separates rounding from Monte Carlo and mask comparisons.
The source is identified as Kupzyk (2011) and credited with the original ordering, moderation, threshold maximum, and usual empirical-versus-exemplary power difference.

findings.location: Table 1, Signed effect, Effect magnitude, Direction, and table note
findings.finding: The signed contrasts, scale, direction, and rounding thresholds are visible. The note separates scientific pattern verdicts from equivalence and distinguishes numerical tolerances from Monte Carlo, mask, and reading uncertainty.
Each row has paired finding content. The ICC cells preserve both the shared .05 maximum and the skew contrast at higher ICC, and the sign-count cells preserve denominators.

layout: All 12 pages are readable. The introduction paragraph and the Section 12 discussion continue onto following pages. Tables and formulae are visually legible. Table 1 and its note fit wholly on page 1.
